counterexamples: A reader that runs while a writer holds the lock receives the previous complete tuple, exactly as a reader that had taken the lock a moment earlier would.

tempting_allegations.allegation: snapshot now reads shared state without the lock, so a request can observe a partially updated route table or race with add/remove.
tempting_allegations.evidence: route_table.py module docstring; add and remove rebind self._routes to a new tuple under the lock in both revisions.
tempting_allegations.why_wrong: snapshot performs one attribute read that yields a complete immutable tuple. Writers never mutate a published tuple; they bind a new one. The base released the lock before its caller iterated, so it gave the same old-or-new guarantee and no more.
